Business.description:
A trader's identity (§ 5b UWG, § 312l BGB): public, so a renter knows
who their contract is with. People never have one.
Business.title: Business

ListingSnapshot.description:
What the listing looked like when it was booked: enough to draw a
booking card without asking the catalog about every row, and the record of
what was actually agreed even if the listing changes or is removed later.
ListingSnapshot.title: ListingSnapshot

Location.description:
Where a listing is (M-5). Stored exactly; answered snapped to a grid of
about 500 m (M-6) until a booking is accepted, like the address.
Location.title: Location

PaymentStart.description:
What the app needs to collect the card: Stripe's client secret for the
PaymentIntent that holds (authorises, not captures) the booking's price.
PaymentStart.title: PaymentStart

get.description:
Find a case: by booking id, by member (id or email, either side), by
status (``disputed``: escalated ones first), or with open claims. Most
recently changed first.

Everything about a booking on one screen: its timeline, the whole
conversation as written (staff see what masking hid), the hand-over
photos as short-lived links, the payment, the dispute and what was
decided. Reading it is logged (H-7).

post.description:
Pay the owner, refund the renter, or refund part. Above the staff
member's limit the resolution waits for a second staff member.
Confirmed means the owner is owed it; collecting it waits for S-9.

get.description: Oldest first: what waits for a second pair of eyes.

post.description:
The second pair of eyes: someone else, whose limit covers the refund
(a lead's does, up to theirs; two leads together, anything).
Not approved: the booking stays in dispute for another decision.

get.description:
What the caller asked for (``role=requester``), is being asked for
(``role=owner``), or both, newest first.

post.description:
Send the same ``Idempotency-Key`` when retrying: a retry returns the
booking the first attempt made, rather than a second booking.

get.description: What cancelling now would refund, shown before anyone confirms.

post.description:
Something went wrong once the booked time began. The payout is held
and the booking no longer completes by itself; support resolves it.

The other side agrees to the offer on the table (the amount is sent
back, so nobody accepts an offer that changed under them).

Either side proposes how much of the price goes back to the renter.
A new offer replaces the one on the table and gives the other side 72
hours to answer.

get.description:
The two sides' hand-over photos, as links that work for a few minutes
(P-27). Staff (with MFA) see them too, to decide disputes; that read is
in the staff audit log (H-7).

schema.title: Response Evidence Bookings  Booking Id  Evidence Get

post.description:
More time straight after the booking, while it is on: a new booking of
the same listing by the same renter, instant if the listing is instant
book, else a request the owner answers. Only if that time is free.

The owner says the thing came back late, within a day of the end. It
becomes a claim staff confirm in the case view; nothing is charged
automatically (that needs a saved card, S-9).

get.description: Oldest first; the cursor continues towards newer messages.

post.description:
The other side never came. Either side reports it about the other, in
the first 2 hours of the booked time, while nobody marked the hand-over.

get.description:
The card step again, for a buyer who left it half way. Payments returns
the same intent however often it is asked.

post.description:
``booking.rated`` feeds the owner's record and becomes a review. It is
dated at the end of the booked window, not when the buyer got round to it.

Two-way reviews: the owner rates the renter after a completed booking,
once. Builds the renter's record other owners see before accepting.

Support tooling (docs/runbook.md): the same rules as the console, with
the support role's limit; ``by`` says who decided.

From the reader: a window booked a moment ago may still show as free,
in which case the booking itself is refused by the constraint.

get.description: Who wrote a reported message (catalog's moderation, FL-7).

post.description: A moderation decision: the words go, the conversation keeps its shape.

get.description:
Everything booking holds about them (GDPR art. 15/20). Hand-over photos
come as links signed for a day, so the file can be saved from them.
Before an account is deleted: is anything still in flight for them?

put.description: No more messages or new bookings between the two of you, either way.
